name: Dal fry
assumptions: Yield estimated from typical dal fry recipes using 1 cup dry dal, which commonly serves 4 people as a main dish with accompaniments like naan.
Total time sums soaking (60 min), cooking dal (~30 min), and tadka/prep steps (~10 min); overlaps possible but conservatively added per instructions.
Ghee classified as dairy (Milk allergen true, Dairy-free false); no eggs, meat, fish, or wheat listed.
Gluten-free true as no barley/rye/wheat/oats; all spices/herbs assumed gluten-free.
Vegan false due to ghee (dairy); Vegetarian true per source and ingredients; Pescatarian true as no meat/fish but dairy present.
No tree nuts, peanuts, soy, or sesame confidently detected; null for sesame due to possible cross-contact in unspecified spice blends like garam masala.
instructions:
Wash and soak toor dal in approx. 3 cups of water, for at least one hours. Dal will be double in volume after soaking. Drain the water.
Cook dal with 2-1/2 cups water and add salt, turmeric, on medium high heat, until soft in texture (approximately 30 mins) it should be like thick soup.
In a frying pan, heat the ghee. Add cumin seeds, and mustard seeds. After the seeds crack, add bay leaves, green chili, ginger and chili powder. Stir for a few seconds.
Add tomatoes, salt and sugar stir and cook until tomatoes are tender and mushy.
Add cilantro and garam masala cook for about one minute.
Pour the seasoning over dal mix it well and cook for another minute.
Serve with Naan.

ingredients.assumptions: Cooking water for dal; plain water contributes zero macros; volume converted using 1 cup = 240 ml.
